title: Permutations
description: Backtracking with a `used[]` flag: at each depth try every unused element. n! results.

notes: Loop from 0 every level — permutations care about order, so any unused index is fair game.
Mirror every state mutation: `used[i] = true` pairs with `used[i] = false`; `push` pairs with `pop`.
Base case fires when `path.length === nums.length` — push a COPY and return.

questions.q: Why does the loop start at 0 every level (unlike Subsets which uses `start`)?
options: Order matters in permutations, so any unused index is valid here
Which indices are already placed in the current path

questions.q: When is the recursion base case reached?
options: Never — backtracking has no base case

exercises.prompt: Fill in the used[] permutations generator.

blanks.hint: how big a full permutation is
un-mark on the way back up

L3.prompt: Write `permute(nums)` returning every ordering of `nums` using a `used[]` boolean array. Log `JSON.stringify(permute([1, 2, 3]))`.
hints: Parallel `used[]` so you can scan every index each level.
Push a copy at the leaf; same array mutates on the way back up.
